metadata.title: Growth mindset mediates perceptions of teachers' and parents' process feedback in digital reading performance: Evidence from 32 OECD countries

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata from 32 OECD countries and applies the final student weight recommended by PISA (W_FSTUWT) to obtain unbiased population parameter estimates. The analytic sample is restricted to students with available data for the variables of interest (TEACHSUP, EMOSUPS, GM, PV1READ, and controls), and the authors treat the PISA reading test scores as missing at random due to the rotated booklet design and random assignment to test forms. Missing values for the five continuous variables (excluding Student Gender) are imputed prior to modeling, and variables are standardized to Z scores. The paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and the mediation is estimated via multilevel structural equation modeling with maximum likelihood.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 data for students in 32 OECD countries who had available data for the variables of interest (teacher process feedback TEACHSUP, parent process feedback EMOSUPS, growth mindset GM, digital reading literacy PV1READ, and controls). The reading literacy outcome is based on the computer-based PISA 2018 reading assessment (1-hour test) with students randomly assigned to electronic test forms; the study uses PV1READ (first plausible value among 10) as the dependent variable. Missingness is handled via expectation-maximization imputation for the five continuous variables (excluding Student Gender), justified by the rotated booklet design and random assignment to booklets.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel mediation (SEM, MLE) with country-specific standardized path coefficients. Total effects: TEACHSUP β range 0.003 to 0.134 (20 countries significant); EMOSUPS β range 0.027 to 0.200 (30 countries significant). Growth mindset direct effect on PV1READ (path b) β range 0.074 to 0.392 across countries (all 32 significant). Direct effects (c’): TEACHSUP significant in 17 countries (β 0.023 to 0.121); EMOSUPS significant in 30 countries (β 0.027 to 0.196).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data (digital reading literacy via PV1READ) from 32 OECD countries, the study leveraged teacher process feedback, parent process feedback, and growth mindset (with gender and ESCS controls) to model digital reading literacy, finding that both teacher and parent process feedback were positively associated with reading performance and that growth mindset had a positive direct effect across all countries (path b βs 0.074–0.392). This indicates that strengthening process-oriented feedback practices and fostering growth-mindset beliefs may support adolescents’ digital reading achievement, though the results are correlational and not causal.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes PISA 2018 computer-based reading data for students in 32 OECD countries, using digital reading literacy measured through plausible values (PV1READ; first of 10 PVs). The authors estimate a multilevel mediation model (SEM with maximum likelihood) to test whether students’ perceptions of teachers’ and parents’ process feedback (TEACHSUP, EMOSUPS) promote growth mindset (GM), which in turn predicts digital reading performance. Across countries, growth mindset shows a consistently positive direct association with PV1READ (path b βs ranging from 0.074 to 0.392), while total effects of process feedback are small but significant in many countries (TEACHSUP significant in 20; EMOSUPS significant in 30). Mediation proportions vary by country (teacher path 4.8%–53.6% in 18 countries; parent path 2.8%–46.8% in 25 countries). Limitations include mild effect sizes, correlational mediation (not causal), and reliance on a single-item growth mindset measure.
